school career== Hauser played basketball, [[golf]] and [[American football|football]] for [[Stevens Point Area Senior High School]] (SPASH) in [[Stevens Point, Wisconsin]].{{cite web |date=March 28, On March 25, 2021, Hauser announced that he would declare for the [[2021 NBA draft]].{{Cite web |date=2021-03-25 |title=UVA's Sam Hauser plans to forgo additional eligibility, turn professional |url=https://richmond.com/sports/college/uvas-sam-hauser-plans-to-forgo-additional-eligibility-turn-professional/article_25c51a6a-1725-5a94-9ef9-26025fe321d5.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210326093113/https://richmond.com/sports/college/uvas-sam-hauser-plans-to-forgo-additional-eligibility-turn-professional/article_25c51a6a-1725-5a94-9ef9-26025fe321d5.html |archive-date=2021-03-26 |access-date=2021-04-06 |website=Richmond}} With Virginia, he posted a 50% FG, 42% 3FG, and 90% FT shooting season but came up just .004 short in [[free throw]] percentage from officially joining the [[50–40–90 club]]. As teammate [[Trey Murphy III]] qualified in the same season, it would have been the first time two teammates made the 50–40–90 club in the same year at the NCAA (or NBA) level of men's basketball competition. ==Professional career== ===Boston Celtics (2021–present)=== After going undrafted in the [[2021 NBA draft]], Hauser signed a two-way contract with the [[Boston Celtics]] on August 13, 2021, splitting time with their G League affiliate, the [[Maine Celtics]].{{cite web|title=Celtics Sign Sam Hauser to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-sam-hauser-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=August 13, 2021|access-date=August 14, 2021|archive-date=August 13, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210813231912/https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-sign-sam-hauser-two-way-contract|url-status=live}} On November 20, 2021, Hauser made his NBA debut in a 111–105 victory over the [[2021–22 Oklahoma City Thunder season|Oklahoma City Thunder]]. On February 11, 2022, his two-way contract was converted into a standard NBA contract.{{cite web |last=Adams |first=Luke |date=February 11, 2022 |title=Celtics Sign Luke Kornet, Promote Sam Hauser |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/02/celtics-plan-to-sign-luke-kornet-promote-sam-hauser.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220211195344/https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2022/02/celtics-plan-to-sign-luke-kornet-promote-sam-hauser.html |archive-date=February 11, 2022 |access-date=February 11, 2022 |website=hoopsrumors.com}} The Celtics reached the [[2022 NBA Finals]] but lost to the [[2021–22 Golden State Warriors season|Golden State Warriors]] in six games despite a 2–1 lead. By making seven threes in the third period, he set a Celtics franchise record for the most three-pointers made in a quarter.{{cite
